## Introduction

Data comes in many formats. In this homework I import data from a text file,
Excel, SPSS, Stata, SAS and a database, using the right package for each.

## Packages

| Package | Used for |
|----|----|
| readxl | Excel files |
| haven | SPSS, Stata and SAS files |
| DBI + RSQLite | Databases |

```{r}
install.packages("haven")
library(haven)

install.packages("DBI")
install.packages("RMariaDB")

library(DBI)
library(RMariaDB)

install.packages("readxl")
library(readxl)
```

## 1. Text file (CSV)

```{r}
iris <- read.csv("iris.csv")
head(iris)
```

## 2. Excel

```{r}
mtcars <- read_excel("mtcars.xlsx")
head(mtcars)
```

## 3. SPSS

```{r}
cars <- read_sav("cars.sav")
head(cars)
```

## 4. Stata

```{r}
mtcars_dta <- read_dta("mtcars.dta")
head(mtcars_dta)
```

## 5. SAS

```{r}
cars_xpt<- read_xpt("cars.xpt")
head(cars_xpt)
```

## 6. Database (SQLite)

```{r}
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "data/school.sqlite")
dbListTables(con)
db_data <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM students")
db_data
dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Conclusion

Base R reads CSV files, `readxl` reads Excel, `haven` reads SPSS, Stata and SAS,
and `DBI` connects R to databases so data can be imported with SQL.
